lines.text: Every time you search your contacts or a shop’s website, a search algorithm runs. Today you’ll write the simplest one — and measure it.
Start at item 1 and check each item in turn.
Stop when you find the target, or when you run out of items.
There’s no point checking more items once you’ve found the target.
A repeat-until with two conditions stops at the right moment.
Algorithms must handle the case where the target isn’t there.
Use a found variable that stays 0 if nothing matches.
Efficiency means how much work an algorithm does.
Count comparisons: in the worst case linear search checks every item.
In Python, linear search is a function that returns the position, or minus one when the target isn’t found.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
